title: The Zimmermann Telegram (1917): the decrypt that changed a war
t: The Zimmermann Telegram (1917): the decrypt that changed a war
description:
In January 1917, British Naval Intelligence decrypted the Zimmermann Telegram — Germany's offer of a military alliance to Mexico against the United States. Britain shared it with Washington; its March 1 publication outraged the American public and helped propel the US into World War I.

The telegram's full decoded text has been public for over a century — one of history's first great signals-intelligence disclosures.

title: Ultra and Magic: WWII codebreaking declassified
t: Ultra and Magic: WWII codebreaking declassified
description:
The Allied breaking of Germany's Enigma (Ultra) and Japan's Purple (Magic) ciphers was among WWII's most closely guarded secrets — kept classified for decades after the war. Declassification in the 1970s revealed that codebreaking had shortened the war by years.

The revelations transformed histories of the Battle of the Atlantic, Midway, and D-Day — intelligence had shaped them all.

description:

VENONA's release rewrote Cold War historiography: historians finally saw what each side knew.

t: CORONA: America's first spy satellites, declassified 1995
description:

The film capsules were snagged mid-air by aircraft — 'catch a falling star' made literal.

description:

The Supreme Court's New York Times Co. v. United States decision protected publication; the full study was declassified in 2011.

They revealed that successive administrations had misled the public about Vietnam — the foundational document of modern press freedom.

The program's targets included Martin Luther King Jr. — the files document the Bureau at its worst.

title: Steamboat Willie enters the public domain (2024)
t: Steamboat Willie enters the public domain (2024)
description:
On January 1, 2024, the 1928 Steamboat Willie version of Mickey Mouse entered the US public domain — copyright's 95-year term expiring. The transition was global news: a corporate icon becoming public property.

The event spotlighted how copyright terms gatekeep culture — and what release looks like.

t: The Great Gatsby enters the public domain (2021)
description:

Each January 1, 'Public Domain Day' releases a new year's harvest.

title: How declassification works: EO 13526
description:
Executive Order 13526 (2009) governs US classification: information is classified only if disclosure would damage national security, for fixed durations, with automatic declassification at 25 years. Anyone can request mandatory review of a document.

The system aims to balance secrecy's necessity against democracy's need to know.

title: FOIA: the public's records tool (1966)
description:
The Freedom of Information Act (1966) lets anyone request federal records; agencies must release them unless an exemption applies. FOIA has pried loose millions of pages — the engine behind countless declassification stories.

Exemptions protect genuine secrets; the presumption favors disclosure.
